question.text: What is the PAN (Permanent Account Number) requirement for investing in mutual funds?

answer.text: PAN is optional for all mutual fund investments
PAN is required only for investments exceeding Rs. 1 lakh

PAN is compulsory for mutual fund investments, with an exemption for small investments / Micro-SIPs up to Rs. 50,000 per investor per year per mutual fund (composite limit covering Micro-SIPs and lump-sum investments)
PAN is required only for equity mutual fund investments

explanation.text: The Logic: PAN is compulsory as part of KYC for mutual fund investments. The exemption is for small investments / Micro-SIPs where the aggregate investment does not exceed Rs. 50,000 per investor per year per mutual fund. This Rs. 50,000 is a composite limit for the small investor's Micro-SIP and lump-sum investments. KYC compliance through a SEBI-registered KRA is still required, typically via PEKRN with an alternate photo ID. The Trap: The Rs. 50,000 limit is per mutual fund (per AMC), not "across all mutual funds", and it is a composite cap covering both Micro-SIPs and any lump-sum investments by the small investor at that fund. Note: Source: NISM Series V-A (Mutual Fund Distributors) workbook, pp.194-195 — Micro-SIP / small-investment PAN exemption with PEKRN/KYC and the composite per-investor-per-year-per-mutual-fund limit.
